situation: My college roommate Sophie's mom died. We haven't talked in a couple of years, but I knew her mom, she used to send us care packages with lemon bars during finals.
reply: Sophie, I'm so sorry about your mom. I still think about those lemon bars showing up every finals week, she fed half our floor. Thinking of you and your dad. No need to reply to this.
note: A years-long gap doesn't need explaining; the specific memory is what she'll keep.

situation: 我手下的员工小李，父亲昨天去世了，他已经请假回老家。我想以领导的身份给他发个微信。
reply: 小李，听说你父亲去世了，非常难过。工作的事一点都不用操心，你手上的项目我已经安排小周接着跟。需要休多久就休多久。想着你和家人，不用回复。
note: 作为领导，最具体的帮助就是把工作接过去，并且明说不用回复。

situation: My best friend Marco's wife Elena died a year ago this Saturday. I want to text him something that day.
reply: Thinking about you and Elena today. I still smile about her making us redo the barbecue because we'd 'insulted the ribs'. I'm around all weekend if you want company. No need to reply.
note: The anniversary message matters more than the first one, because most people have stopped sending them.

situation: 好朋友阿杰的爸爸三周前去世了。我这几周隔几天就发消息问他怎么样，昨天他回我：我没事，别老问了。我有点慌，不知道还要不要再联系他。
reply: 好，我不追着问了。我在，不会走开。周六下午我把你爱吃的老街卤味挂你家门把手上，不用开门，也不用回我。
note: 被推开时不辩解也不消失：接受他的话，把“问候”换成不需要回应的陪伴。之后隔一两周发一句，不带问题。

situation: 同事阿May养了13年的狗豆豆昨天走了，她今天请了假。我们关系不错，我见过豆豆几次，它每次都叼着拖鞋来迎人。想在微信上跟她说一声。
reply: 阿May，听说豆豆走了，真的很难过。我一直记得它叼着拖鞋跑来迎人的样子，13年，它在你身边过得特别幸福。工作这边你别惦记，周三的周会我帮你汇报。不用回我，就是想着你。
note: 宠物离世也是真的失去：叫它的名字，说一个具体的记忆，给一个实际的帮助，并明说不用回复。

situation: Soy gestora autónoma. Mi clienta de hace ocho años, Pilar, me escribió que su marido Andrés murió el sábado y que se va a retrasar con los papeles del trimestre, que vencen el 20 de octubre.
reply: Pilar, lo siento muchísimo por Andrés. Me acuerdo de lo orgulloso que estaba cuando abrió el segundo taller en 2022. Del trimestre no te preocupes: presento yo la declaración del 20 de octubre con lo que ya tengo, y lo que falte lo vemos en noviembre. No hace falta que me contestes.
note: Con una clienta, la oferta concreta es quitarle el trabajo de encima, no ofrecer ayuda en general.

situation: My sister-in-law Amy texted me that she lost the baby at 11 weeks. She and my brother had only told close family. I have no idea what to say.
reply: Amy, I'm so sorry. Thank you for telling me. There's nothing you need to say or do, and you don't have to be okay. I'll leave a pot of soup on your step Thursday evening; no need to answer the door or reply to this.
note: Don't explain the loss ('at least it was early', 'it wasn't meant to be'); presence plus one practical thing is the whole message.

situation: Our elderly neighbour Margaret's husband Frank died last week. We're not close with her, but Frank waved at our kids from the porch every morning and once fixed my son's bike without being asked. I want to leave a card in her mailbox.
reply:
Dear Margaret,
We were so sorry to hear about Frank. Our boys still call him 'the waving man'; every morning on the way to school he was on the porch, and he once spent a whole Saturday fixing Theo's bike chain without being asked. Our street won't be the same. Tom will bring your bins in on Thursday evenings for as long as it helps. No need to reply to this card.
With love,
Anna, Tom, Theo and Max
note: A neighbour you barely know still gets the name, one specific memory and one practical thing that needs no answer from her.

situation: I just found out on LinkedIn that my former manager Denise's husband Paul died in July. It's been over two months and I feel awful I didn't say anything. I met Paul at our team Christmas parties.
reply: Denise, I only just heard about Paul, and I'm so sorry. I still remember him at our team Christmas parties, the only person who could get the whole finance team onto the dance floor. Thinking of you. No need to reply to this.
note: Late is fine, and often lands better, because the messages have dried up by month two. One clause for the timing, no paragraph of guilt.

situation: I'm going to the funeral of my coworker Dev's father on Friday. I never met his dad, but Dev talked about him a lot, especially how they went to every cricket test at Edgbaston together. What do I actually say to Dev in the line after the service?
reply: Dev, I'm so sorry about your dad. I keep thinking about the two of you at Edgbaston every summer. You don't need to say anything, I just wanted to be here.
note: In a receiving line, two or three sentences. If you never met the person, something the griever told you about them does the work of a memory.

situation: 一起共事了十年的同事老周上周突发心梗走了。我没见过他太太，想请同事转一封信给她，说说老周在单位是什么样的人。
reply: 周太太您好，我是老周在设计院的同事李明，和他共事了十年。听到消息，我们都很难过。老周是我们组最靠得住的人，谁的图纸出了问题，他都会留下来陪着改到半夜，第二天还拎一兜包子来。他常说起您和女儿，说周末最盼的就是一家人去爬紫金山。我们都会记得他。单位这边的手续，您告诉王主任一声，我们来跑。您不用回信。
note: 写给不认识的家属，最珍贵的是具体的往事和他在别人眼里的样子；先说明自己是谁，免去回复。

situation: 从小一起长大的好朋友婷婷，她奶奶昨天在老家去世了，婷婷是奶奶带大的。小时候我去她家，奶奶总给我们一人塞一个煮鸡蛋。我在德国读书赶不回去，想给她发一段语音。
reply: 婷婷，是我。刚听说奶奶走了，我真的很难过。我一直记得小时候去你家，奶奶每次都给我们一人塞一个煮鸡蛋，还说读书费脑子。这次我赶不回去，但我一直想着你。你不用回我，也不用回电话。周六你那边晚上八点我给你打过去，不想接就不接，一点关系都没有。
note: 赶不回去时，语音比文字更像陪伴：一句带过自己不能到场，不讲自己的愧疚，说出奶奶的一个具体记忆，再约一个可以不接的电话。

situation: My friend Kara's younger brother Josh died by suicide last week. I met Josh a few times; at her birthday last year he spent ages teaching me to make proper espresso. I don't know what to say or whether to mention how he died.
reply: Kara, I'm so sorry about Josh. I keep thinking of him at your birthday, patiently teaching me to pull an espresso shot and laughing at my first three attempts. I'm dropping dinner at yours on Thursday evening, no need to answer the door. You don't have to reply to this, I'm just here.
note: Say his name and a real memory, don't ask what happened or offer explanations, and if she brings up how he died, follow her lead.

situation: My teammate Rosa comes back to the office on Monday after three weeks off; her mum died of cancer. We sit next to each other and she used to tell me about her mum's allotment. What do I say when she walks in?
reply: Rosa, welcome back. I'm so sorry about your mum. I keep thinking of her and those allotment courgettes you used to bring in. I've put the Hendry notes from the last three weeks in one doc, so you don't have to dig through your inbox. No need to talk about any of it unless you want to.
note: First day back: say it once, briefly, then let her decide whether it comes up again; catching her up on work is the concrete help.

situation: My friend Tariq was laid off yesterday after 11 years at the same engineering firm, one of 40 cuts. He posted about it on LinkedIn, but I want to text him privately. When I was job hunting two years ago, he rebuilt my whole CV in one evening.
reply: Tariq, I'm so sorry about the layoff. Eleven years, and you were always the one people went to when something was on fire. You rebuilt my whole CV in one evening when I needed it, so I'm returning the favour: I'm free Sunday afternoon to go through yours with you, or just to get a beer and not talk about it at all. No need to reply today.
note: A job loss is a loss too: no silver linings or 'it's their loss', just one specific quality, one concrete offer and no pressure to answer.

situation: My ex-boyfriend Tom's mum, Janet, died on Sunday. We broke up two years ago on okay terms, and I was close to her; she taught me to make her Sunday roast. I want to text Tom without it seeming like I'm trying to get back into his life.
reply: Tom, I'm so sorry about your mum. I'll always remember Janet teaching me her Sunday roast. I was lucky to know her. No need to reply, I'm just thinking of you and your family.
note: From an ex, skip the concrete offer: a short message that asks for nothing is the kind one.

situation: My friend Nadia's father died on Monday. She hadn't spoken to him in six years because of how he treated her mum, and she just texted me 'I don't even know what I'm supposed to feel.' We've been friends since uni.
reply: Nadia, I'm so sorry. There's no supposed to here: sad, relieved, angry, numb, or all of it in one afternoon, it all makes sense. You don't have to sort it out or explain it to anyone, me included. I'm around all weekend if you want company, and no need to reply to this.
note: When the relationship with the person who died was painful, don't assume grief or praise them; give permission for whatever she feels.

situation: In our class parents' WhatsApp group, Olga posted that her husband Viktor died suddenly on Sunday. Dozens of people are replying with heart emojis. Her daughter Mila and mine are best friends, and Viktor coached their Saturday netball team and always stayed after practice to feed balls to any girl who wanted extra shooting. I want to message her privately.
reply: Olga, I'm so sorry about Viktor. The girls adored him, and I'll always picture him staying after practice to feed balls to anyone who wanted extra shots. Mila is welcome at ours any afternoon this week or next, just tell me which days suit. No need to reply to this. Thinking of you both.
note: After a group announcement, a private message with one real memory and an easy, concrete offer stands out from the emoji wall.

situation: 我是初二（5）班班主任。学生小宇的爸爸上周五去世了，小宇请了一周假，下周一回学校。他爸爸每次家长会都来，坐第一排认真记笔记。我打算让课代表帮小宇补这周落下的课，想给小宇妈妈发条微信。
reply: 小宇妈妈您好，听到小宇爸爸去世的消息，我非常难过。每次家长会他都坐在第一排认真记笔记，我一直记得。小宇下周一回来，这周落下的课我会让课代表帮他补上，学习上的事您先不用操心，我也会多留意他在学校的状态。您不用回复这条消息。
note: 老师的身份决定了具体帮助落在学校这一边，不打听家里的情况。

situation: 我姑姑前天因病去世了，她儿子是我表哥阿峰。我从小寒暑假都住在姑姑家，她每年都给我包荠菜馄饨。我自己也很难过，但想先给表哥发个微信。周六追悼会，我可以提前过去帮忙招呼亲戚。
reply: 哥，姑姑走了，我心里也特别难受。我一直记得每年寒暑假住在你们家，姑姑包的荠菜馄饨。周六追悼会我早点过去，帮你招呼亲戚，你不用操心这块。不用回我。
note: 自己也在难过时，一句带过自己的感受就好，重点放在他身上，再给一个具体的帮忙。

situation: 高中好友小楠在多伦多读博，她外婆前天在老家去世了，她因为签证的事回不去参加葬礼。葬礼是北京时间10月4日周日上午9点，她那边是10月3日周六晚上9点。高中时我常去她外婆家，外婆每次都端出自己做的桂花糕，说我们太瘦了。
reply: 小楠，听说外婆走了，我真的很难过。我一直记得高中去外婆家，她端出一大盘桂花糕，非说我们太瘦。不能回去送她，这份难受一定特别重，你不用在谁面前撑着。周六你那边晚上9点，葬礼开始的时候，我给你打视频陪着你，不想接就不接。不用回我。
note: 亲人葬礼回不去的人，最难熬的是葬礼那个时刻：陪她度过那一刻，比一句安慰更具体。

situation: My sister-in-law Karen died of cancer last week. Her daughter, my niece Lily, is 15, and she and I have a thing of going to the secondhand bookshop together; Karen always dropped her at mine and honked twice when she came to collect her. I want to message Lily directly, not just her dad.
reply: Lily, I'm so sorry about your mum. I keep thinking of her honking twice outside my place when she came to get you after the bookshop. Whenever you want, I'd love to take you to the bookshop again, and we don't have to talk about anything. You don't need to reply to this, not now and not ever.
note: To a teenager, write to them directly and simply; offering the thing you already share beats a general 'I'm here for you'.

situation: My friend Priya's best friend Anjali died in a car crash on Saturday; they'd been friends since they were 11. Priya told me she feels silly being so wrecked because 'it's not like she was family'. I met Anjali at Priya's 30th, where her speech had the whole room crying with laughter.
reply: Priya, I'm so sorry about Anjali. Friends since you were 11 is family in every way that counts, and you don't need anyone's permission to be wrecked. I'll never forget her speech at your 30th, the whole room crying with laughter. I'm dropping dinner at yours on Thursday evening, no need to answer the door. You don't have to reply to this.
note: When the loss isn't family, people feel they have no right to grieve; say once that they do, then the memory and the offer.

situation: 取引先の田中部長から、お母様が9月29日に亡くなられたので来週はお休みする、とメールがありました。去年の打ち合わせのとき、部長がお母様の漬けた梅干しをお土産にくださいました。10月8日（木）の定例会議は私が主催しているので、延期するつもりです。
reply:
田中部長
このたびはお母様のご逝去の報に接し、心よりお悔やみ申し上げます。昨年お土産にいただいたお母様の梅干しの味を、今もよく覚えております。10月8日（木）の定例会議はこちらで延期いたしますので、お仕事のことはどうかお気になさらず、ご家族とのお時間を大切になさってください。ご返信には及びません。
note: ビジネスでも一つの具体的な思い出と、自分で決められる仕事の配慮だけを書き、「重ね重ね」などの忌み言葉は避けます。

situation: I'm Dr. Amara Bello, a vet at Larkfield Vet Clinic. Yesterday we put Mr. Okoye's 16-year-old cat, Pepper, to sleep; he'd brought her in every year since she was a kitten, and she always purred on the exam table. We send a handwritten card, and we'll post Pepper's clay paw print to his home next week.
reply:
Dear Mr. Okoye,
All of us at Larkfield were so sorry to say goodbye to Pepper yesterday. Sixteen years of check-ups, and she purred on the exam table every single time, which hardly any cat does. We'll post her clay paw print to you next week, so there's nothing you need to do. No need to reply to this card.
With warm wishes,
Dr. Amara Bello and the Larkfield team
note: From a business, the card is only for him: no invoice, no reminders, no booking prompts.

situation: Ollie in my online D&D group posted in our Discord that his mum died on Tuesday. We've played every Wednesday night for three years but never met in person, and he once told us she taught him to play with her old dice. I run the game and want to DM him.
reply: Ollie, I'm so sorry about your mum. I keep thinking about you telling us she taught you to play with her old dice, so in a way she's been at our table every Wednesday for three years. Don't give the campaign a thought; I'll tell the group we're pausing until you're ready to come back, whenever that is. No need to reply.
note: An online-only friendship is still a real one: the memory can be something he told you, and the concrete offer is the thing you actually share.

situation: My colleague Ben Adler's father, Saul, died on Sunday. Ben's email says the family is sitting shiva at his home through Thursday 8 October, visitors welcome 7 to 9pm. I'm not Jewish and have never been to a shiva. Saul came to our office summer picnic last year and spent the whole afternoon teaching the interns backgammon. I want to text Ben that I'd like to come on Tuesday evening.
reply: Ben, I'm so sorry about your dad. I keep thinking of Saul at the summer picnic, spending the whole afternoon teaching the interns backgammon. I'd like to come by on Tuesday evening during the shiva hours, just to be there with you. No need to reply to this.
note: At a shiva, follow the mourners' lead: let them speak first, keep it short, and ask a family friend before bringing any food.

situation: Mon amie Léa a perdu son compagnon Hugo dans un accident de vélo il y a dix jours. Le jour même, je lui ai écrit « il est dans un monde meilleur » et elle m'a répondu sèchement « non, il devrait être ici ». Hugo jouait de la guitare à chacun de nos pique-niques au bord du canal, et je voudrais lui réécrire sans tout aggraver.
reply: Léa, tu as raison, il devrait être ici, et ma phrase de l'autre jour n'était pas juste. Pardon. Je pense à Hugo et à sa guitare à chacun de nos pique-niques au bord du canal. Samedi midi, je dépose un repas devant ta porte, pas besoin d'ouvrir ni de me répondre.
note: Après une maladresse, on la reconnaît en une phrase sans se justifier, puis on revient à Hugo et à une aide concrète.

situation: My dad, Frank, is 72, and his best friend of 50 years, Ray, died on Monday. They fished at Miller's Pond every Saturday morning for as long as I can remember, and Ray taught me to bait a hook. Dad doesn't do big feelings talk, I live three hours away, and I'm visiting the weekend of 10 October.
reply: Dad, I'm so sorry about Ray. Fifty years of Saturday mornings at Miller's Pond, and he was the one who taught me to bait a hook. I'm coming up the weekend of the 10th; if you fancy it, we could go down to the pond on the Saturday morning, and we don't have to talk unless you want to. You don't need to call me back.
note: Comforting a parent: name their friend and the ritual they shared, offer side-by-side company rather than a big talk, and ask for nothing back.

situation: 我是研究生，导师王老师的爱人李阿姨上周因病去世了。每年中秋李阿姨都请我们课题组去家里吃她包的饺子，还总让我们打包带走。王老师这周请假了，我和师兄小陈商量好，这两周实验室的日常和师弟师妹的问题由我们俩先盯着。想给王老师发条微信。
reply: 王老师，听说李阿姨走了，我们都很难过。每年中秋去您家，李阿姨包的饺子我们吃完还要打包带走，她的热情我们一直记得。实验室这边您不用操心，这两周的日常和师弟师妹的问题，我和小陈师兄先盯着。您和家人多保重，不用回复。
note: 学生给导师写：一个具体的记忆，加上自己真能做到的帮助，不打听，也不提论文进度。
